content: This shift requires consulting firms to move beyond standard extraction advisory and develop specialized competencies in downstream processing, technological integration, and advanced value-chain optimization. The adoption of the G20 Critical Minerals Framework under South Africa’s presidency in 2026 represents a transformative initiative targeting improved governance and sustainability across the sector [14] . Concurrently, the integration of advanced technologies has become a cornerstone of modern mining strategies, prompting consulting firms to rapidly expand their technological advisory capabilities. The modern competitor landscape is characterized by a race to offer integrated digital solutions, where consultants advise on the deployment of artificial intelligence, automated machinery, and comprehensive digital management systems. At the operational level, consulting firms are also adapting to specific technological advances championed by mining operators. While specific insights remain sparse, pieces of information highlight notable advances, such as the achievements of companies like Tharisa in advancing underground mining techniques as part of future-driven strategies [21] . Consultants must possess the technical acumen to advise on such specialized underground methodologies to remain competitive [21] . Moreover, market positioning is increasingly influenced by corporate social responsibility and diversity initiatives. Events such as the collaborative webinar by WiMSA and the Minerals Council South Africa celebrating women in mining, while not directly informing technical consulting trends, reflect the evolving corporate culture and governance standards that consulting firms must embody and advise upon [22] .
